title.narrative: Tanzania Country Programme

description.narrative: TradeMark Africa's Tanzania Country Programme works to leverage Tanzania's unique geography (bordered by eight countries and anchored to the Indian Ocean through the Port of Dar es Salaam, Tanga, and Mtwara), to position it as a competitive trade and transit hub for East, Central, and Southern Africa, building on over fourteen years of engagement since 2011. The Programme spans physical infrastructure, including One Stop Border Post construction and operationalisation at Tunduma, Kabanga, Mutukula, and Holili, and port modernisation at Dar es Salaam, alongside a comprehensive digital trade systems agenda covering the Tanzania Mercantile Exchange (TMX), the Mifugo Integrated Management Information System (MIMS) for livestock and fisheries, the Agricultural Trade Management Information System (ATMIS), and single window modules across standards, medicines, and investment. Complementing this, the Programme strengthens Tanzania's trade and investment environment through implementation support for the 2024 National Trade Policy, improves export competitiveness in high-potential value chains such as horticulture, grains, livestock, and seaweed in Zanzibar, with targeted SPS and standards capacity building, and promotes inclusive trade through digital financial access, market linkage tools, and dedicated women-in-trade programmin

receiver-org.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) is a leading Aid-for-Trade organisation founded in 2010 to grow intra-African trade, increase Africa’s share in global trade, and make trade more pro-poor and sustainable. We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.

title.narrative: Claim processing time as a result of digitisation of the Warehouse Receipt System
Reduction in permit issuance time on the Mifugo Integrated Management System in Tanzania (MIMS)

comment.narrative: 99% reduction in permit issuance time on the Mifugo Integrated Management System in Tanzania (MIMS), from 14 days in July 2022 to 1 hour in June 2024, and 100% increase in government revenue collection from the system, $12M revenue generated by the system.
